questions.solution:
In the sentence "You can buy a plastic cover to put into your computer if you’re worried about dust". The correct option is 1.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

I couldn't hear what was she saying due to the noise of the planes taking off.

options.text: due to the noise of the

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"what was she saying". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the word **order of the reported speech or indirect question **within the sentence.
 
• In indirect questions, the correct syntax does not invert the subject and the auxiliary verb as in direct questions.
 
• The sentence mistakenly follows the structure of **a direct question ("What was she saying?") within **an indirect statement.
 
• The correct structure should be **"what she was saying" **instead of **"what was she saying." **
 
• This order aligns with standard English grammar rules for constructing indirect questions/statements.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "I couldn't hear" sets up the sentence without any error, indicating the speaker's inability to hear.
 
• "Due to the noise of the" correctly introduces the cause of not being able to hear.
 
• "Planes taking off" correctly ends the sentence with a participle phrase describing the source of the noise, without any grammatical errors.

questions.question:
Select the antonym of the given word.

Notorious
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Notorious** means famous or well known, typically for some bad quality or deed. (प्रसिद्ध आमतौर पर किसी खराब गुणवत्ता या कार्य के लिए)

 
 
• For eg- This place is **notorious **for the drugs.
 
 
 
• **Efficient **means achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense. (न्यूनतम व्यर्थ प्रयास या व्यय के साथ अधिकतम उत्पादकता प्राप्त करना)
 
• **Infamous **means well known for some bad quality or deed. (कुछ खराब गुणवत्ता या काम के लिए जाना जाता है)
 
• **Optimistic **means hopeful and confident about the future. (भविष्य के प्रति आशावान और आश्वस्त)
 
• **Popular** means liked or admired by many people or by a particular person or group. It is always used in a positive sense. (कई लोगों द्वारा या किसी विशेष व्यक्ति या समूह द्वारा पसंद या प्रशंसा की गई। **इसका प्रयोग हमेशा सकारात्मक अर्थ में किया जाता है**)
 
 
• For eg- She was among the **popular **girls of the school.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• You may think that the correct answer is Infamous but infamous is the **synonym **of Notorious. (आप सोच सकते हैं कि सही उत्तर Infamous (बदनाम) है लेकिन Infamous (बदनाम), notorious (कुख्यात) का पर्याय है)
 
• **Notorious **and **popular **are **antonyms **of each other because** 'notorious'** means **someone who is well-known for a bad quality** whereas** 'popular' **means **someone who is well-known for some good quality.** (कुख्यात (notorious) और लोकप्रिय (popular) एक-दूसरे के विलोम हैं क्योंकि 'कुख्यात' का अर्थ है कोई ऐसा व्यक्ति जो खराब गुणवत्ता के लिए जाना जाता है जबकि 'लोकप्रिय' का अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो किसी अच्छी गुणवत्ता के लिए जाना जाता है)
 
• Thus, '**popular**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.**

If you play your cards right, the job could be your when she leaves.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2) i.e. 'the job could be your'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct possessive form should be **"yours," **not **"your."**

 
 
• **Example**: "The job can be yours."
 
 
 
• "Your" is an adjective that needs to describe a noun, but in this context, we need a possessive pronoun.
 
• **"Can"** is more appropriate than **"could" **in this context because "can" indicates a strong possibility or potential, making the sentence more assertive.

Therefore, the correct sentence is- ***"If you play your cards right, the job can be yours when she leaves."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option (1): "If you play" is grammatically correct as it sets up the conditional clause.
 
• Explanation: It starts the sentence properly for a conditional statement.
 
• Option (3): "when she leaves" is grammatically correct as it provides the condition under which the job becomes available.
 
• Explanation: This clause correctly specifies a future event.
 
• Option (4): "your cards right" is grammatically correct as it completes the idiomatic expression properly.
 
• Explanation: It adheres correctly to the idiom and its usage in context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

She has decided __on to do__ a Chinese language course.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

With the preposition 'on' we cannot use another preposition. The use of preposition 'to' after 'on' is grammatically incorrect. So, 'to' should be omitted.

Also, the preposition 'on' must be followed with the continuous form of verb i.e. doing.

So, the correct phrase would be **'on doing'.**

Option 1 is correct.

questions.question:

There is no point of arguing over something so unimportant.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The use of preposition 'of' in option 2 is incorrect. 'Of' is used to indicate a cause of something. 'In' can be used for the inclusion or expressing the part of an activity.

The correct phrase should be 'point in arguing'.

All other options are grammatically correct.

So, option 2 is correct.

questions.question:

Swift
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

**Swift** means happening quickly or promptly.

For eg- He had a swift recovery.

Harsh means unpleasantly rough or jarring to the senses.

Slow means moving or operating, or designed to do so, only at a low speed; not quick or fast.

**Quick** means moving fast or doing something in a short time.

For eg- She had to reach her office very quick.

So, option 4 is correct.
